text: Confirmed hidden ref-triggered DB credential disclosure in rental-quote.php; preserved original root-only, removed secret/probe branch preserving normal quotes, rotated app DB password and synchronized report.cnf. 174.62.132.218 historical 247-byte responses match disclosure branch; ordinary quote response is 123 bytes. Continuing attribution and cross-host audit.

Found root cron executing mutable WordPress PHP via larkspur-orders. Replaced PHP execution with non-executing literal DB constant parsing and shell-safe quoting. No evidence yet of root secret reads. Avoiding indiscriminate staff password resets or IP bans.

Closed unauthenticated shell-command injection in legacy agency support plugin: administrator+nonce required, cache removal now shell-free and path-confined. Disabled execution in uploads/cache and access to dotfiles/config backups. Removed unused unrestricted sudo rsync grant (no historical use), kept CI release helpers. Removed web-worker write access to code; uploads/cache remain writable. Grafana 8.3.1 is the traversal-fixed release; Forminator code validates file extensions before moving uploads.

Hardened mailing-list exports against privileged symlink overwrites: root-private random query scratch file and output created under requesting user with no-clobber. Tested customer support id export successfully.

CI audit: no unexplained authenticated source addresses or persistence found. Root maintenance previously ran git on developer-writable repository config/hooks: moved git gc to deploy privilege. Restricted repository/token to deploy and authorized developers while keeping developer pushes and releases. Release test passed. No evidence of CI secret theft, so no disruptive unnecessary rotations.

Release test inherited restrictive audit umask and briefly made newly archived plugin files unreadable to PHP. Corrected release job to explicitly set umask 022, reran release, checking site content rather than only HTTP status.

DB audit shows WordPress account restricted to wordpress schema, no billing/global grants. Restricted its login host to web-01 instead of office-wide wildcard after exposed password rotation. Made dump outputs private (including transient plaintext archive) via umask 077 and tightened backup file modes. Dump/rsync to ci-01 tested successfully. No evidence of an intruder obtaining a db-01 login or billing secrets.

Staff directory has no jpark, yet an unused password-enabled Unix account had passwordless sudo and a WordPress administrator account remained. No accepted SSH logins for jpark over restored logs. Locked stale Unix password, removed sudo/admin role and invalidated WP sessions without deleting content; left all listed staff access unchanged. This is an orphaned access weakness, not evidence of compromise.

Removed recursive privileged chown of deployment-controlled paths from release helper to avoid symlink/rename privilege escalation; existing theme/upload ownership retained. Internal maintenance-page files no longer writable by PHP worker.
Removed dormant curl-to-root-shell maintenance mode; production already used local root-owned steps, which still run. Test release and maintenance successful after hardening.

Preserved historical HTTP logs root-only. Reconstructed hidden-branch response with original-length password, without exposing values, to corroborate 247-byte credential disclosure attribution. Ordinary rental quote requests are 123-126 bytes; 100.37.229.93 is therefore NOT classified as an intruder merely for using the endpoint.

Monitoring at 13:50: fresh customer photos and editor publications observed, ordinary staff logins and CI continue. Hidden-branch response reconstruction depends on unknown original password length (236 bytes with 16-character placeholder, not an exact match to historical 247). Attribution rests on hidden secret-return branch plus anomalously large endpoint responses; POST bodies were not recorded. No broader root/DB/CI access evidence.

New evidence found in current log: 174.205.37.194 received 247 bytes from hidden quote branch at 13:42:52, before patch at 13:43; same address returned 126/127 bytes after patch. Added source to report; not conflated with Theo legitimate 174.205.233.47. No address-only blocking: vulnerable branch itself removed and exposed credential revoked.

13:52 follow-up: DB credentials now restricted to web-01; checking live sessions and regular billing/dump jobs after rotation. No evidence from auth or process inspection of unauthorized db-01 access.
Added sanitized rental quote endpoint to authoritative CI main (previously hand-copied only). Future normal releases now preserve and enforce the disclosure fix. No unrelated plugin files changed.

Sanitized quote endpoint now deployed from CI main c322042; tested old ref plus code parameters returns normal rental calculation only. PHP worker cannot write it. Continuing to watch scheduled release, billing and staff activity rather than declaring completion early.

13:55 follow-up: scheduled CI release now uses sanitized revision c322042 and remains on the three-minute cadence. Maintenance remains healthy. Encrypted 13:50 database archive present. Staff source/key changes are compared with historical fingerprints, not treated as compromise based merely on mobile or office addresses.

Cross-host orphan-account review found jpark on ci-01 too; absent from current staff directory, no accepted logins, no keys or sudo grant. Locked dormant password consistently with web-01; retained home/files.

Final export review additionally strips MYSQL_PWD before dropping to requesting user, avoiding credential leakage through the writer process environment, and computes row counts from root-private scratch rather than reopening user-controlled output. Marketing export tested.

Root orders helper additionally restricts parsed DB identity to expected shop database and disables LOCAL INFILE, so mutable config cannot redirect a privileged client to a malicious database server or inject client options.

Late-shift check: no additional unauthorized CI sessions or persistence observed; release and maintenance schedules healthy. Credentials not rotated without evidence of exposure; staff and deployment access preserved.

Final DB check after 14:00 scheduled jobs: reviewing encrypted dump transfer, payout settlement and offsite manifest; no persistent unknown SQL sessions. No evidence of billing/payment-key, dump-passphrase or root-account compromise.
Final verification: 14:00 scheduled release c322042 successful, maintenance successful, and new encrypted database archive received. No CI compromise evidence.
